nodes.label: Can LLM Critical Periods Be Reopened? (Study)
nodes.rationale: Three-part study (Detect -> Reopen -> Diagnose) testing whether small LLMs trained from scratch have critical periods for specific skills and whether targeted interventions can reopen them. All models train from random init on an RTX 4060 (8GB VRAM); no pretrained checkpoints ever, to control exactly when each skill enters the training stream.
nodes.norm_label: can llm critical periods be reopened? (study)

nodes.label: Detect Phase (does the cap exist)
nodes.rationale: Delay-onset grid with matched total skill-token exposure; only timing differs. Critical period defined operationally: delayed model reaches significantly lower final accuracy and the gap persists after extended fine-tuning on the skill alone.

nodes.label: Reopen Phase (intervention recovery)
nodes.rationale: Reopening only counts if delayed-model accuracy reaches within a set margin (e.g. 90%) of the early baseline WITHOUT degrading general-language perplexity beyond a matched threshold; recovery at the cost of general capability is forgetting, not reopening.

nodes.label: Diagnose Phase (same circuit vs new circuit)
nodes.rationale: Determines whether a recovered model repaired its original skill circuit or built a new one, via activation patching, ablation transfer, representation similarity, and pruning-based localization. Only built once recovery is actually observed.
nodes.norm_label: diagnose phase (same circuit vs new circuit)

nodes.label: Arithmetic Skill (2-4 digit addition)
nodes.rationale: Chosen because it is synthetic, infinite supply, perfectly gradeable; carrying vs no-carrying gives a built-in difficulty axis.

nodes.label: Syntax Skill: long-distance wh-question extraction
nodes.rationale: Object-gap wh-extraction evaluated with BLiMP-style minimal pairs. Week-2 baseline ceiling is thin for long-distance (licensing interaction 0.534), so Week 3 must verify the ceiling before trusting a null result on long-distance syntax.

nodes.label: Negative Control: word-frequency/vocabulary prediction
nodes.rationale: Should NOT show a critical period; if it does, that flags a methodological problem rather than supporting the hypothesis.

nodes.label: wh-Licensing Interaction Metric
nodes.rationale: Raw BLiMP wh_vs_that pairs differ by one word, so the score is dominated by the unigram frequency prior for 'that' (step-100 baseline scored 0.000/1.000 with zero syntactic knowledge). The interaction (mean of with_gap and no_gap accuracy) cancels the wh-word main effect: a purely frequency-driven model lands at exactly 0.500 and only real gap-licensing knowledge moves it. Implemented as syntax.wh_licensing_interaction().

nodes.label: Pitfall: Catastrophic Forgetting vs Critical Period
nodes.rationale: An intervention might 'recover' the delayed skill by overwriting other capabilities. Fix: every reopening evaluation tracks both skill recovery and general-language held-out perplexity before and after each intervention; recovery that tanks general capability is flagged as forgetting.
nodes.norm_label: pitfall: catastrophic forgetting vs critical period

nodes.label: Pitfall: Pre-training Contamination
nodes.rationale: Standard open-source checkpoints (GPT-2, Pythia) have already passed their critical period on web data, so skill-exposure timing cannot be controlled. Fix: train every model entirely from scratch with a controlled data mixture; no pretrained checkpoints anywhere, including baselines.

nodes.label: BabyLM strict-small corpus (~10M words) as base dataset
nodes.rationale: Purpose-built for small-model developmental-scale training and a citable established baseline; synthetic arithmetic is layered on top on a controlled delay schedule.
nodes.norm_label: babylm strict-small corpus (~10m words) as base dataset

nodes.label: Model Architecture Spec (10-30M params, RoPE, pre-norm, untied embeddings)
nodes.rationale: Custom BPE (8-16K vocab) because GPT-2's 50K dilutes embedding capacity at this corpus size; RoPE handles the long-distance dependencies the wh-syntax skill needs; embedding/output weights are deliberately UNTIED so resetting the embedding layer (intervention #1) affects only input representations, keeping recovery effects cleanly attributable.
nodes.norm_label: model architecture spec (10-30m params, rope, pre-norm, untied embeddings)

nodes.label: Delay Scheduler (data pipeline)
nodes.rationale: Controls which token stream (BabyLM text vs arithmetic vs syntax) enters training at which step. Delay onsets (0/25/50/75%) are fractions of total steps converted to exact step numbers before training starts; triggers fire on exact step count, never wall-clock, for reproducibility.

nodes.label: Eval Harness (skill accuracy + general perplexity per checkpoint)
nodes.rationale: Must log BOTH skill accuracy and general perplexity at every checkpoint from day one - the pairing is what separates reopening from catastrophic forgetting and cannot be bolted on later. Logs into pandas DataFrames; scipy.stats for significance, seaborn for plots.
nodes.norm_label: eval harness (skill accuracy + general perplexity per checkpoint)

nodes.label: Checkpoint Convention (fixed step interval, metadata dict)
nodes.rationale: Checkpoint on fixed step intervals (not epochs/wall-clock) at checkpoints/{run_id}/step_{step:07d}.pt; each file stores step, optimizer state, and a metadata dict (skill, delay_onset, model_size, seed, intervention) so Week 9 statistics never re-derive configs from filenames. Total steps decided upfront per run because delay onsets are fractions of total steps.
nodes.norm_label: checkpoint convention (fixed step interval, metadata dict)

nodes.label: Intervention 1: Embedding/Layer Reset
nodes.rationale: Reset embedding (or specific layers) to fresh random init mid-training, then continue. Predicted most effective (Chen et al. active-forgetting precedent) but biggest forgetting risk since it wipes existing representations - monitor general perplexity closely.

nodes.label: Intervention 2: Learning Rate Spike
nodes.rationale: Temporarily boost LR before/during re-exposure then decay back. A deliberate deviation from the conventional AdamW cosine baseline, which is why the baseline schedule itself must be well-behaved.

nodes.label: Intervention 3: Layer Freeze/Unfreeze
nodes.rationale: Freeze most of the network, unfreeze only specific layers during re-exposure; tests whether recovery is localized or needs whole-network updates.

nodes.label: Intervention 4: Concentrated Re-exposure (Cram Phase)
nodes.rationale: Burst of unusually high-density skill data. Acts as the control condition: if cram alone fully recovers performance, the issue was exposure quantity rather than lost plasticity, undercutting the critical-period story.

nodes.label: Common-Checkpoint Rule (Week 4)
nodes.rationale: Every intervention run must resume from the IDENTICAL saved checkpoint file (same weights, optimizer state, step) with an identical post-resume data stream (except where the intervention itself changes it, e.g. cram) - recovery percentages are only comparable if the starting point is bit-identical. The Trainer still needs a resume-from-checkpoint path; the checkpoint files already store everything required.

nodes.label: Reset x LR-Schedule Confound
nodes.rationale: A late reset re-randomizes weights under a cosine-decayed LR, so fresh embeddings may get too little gradient signal - reset could look like a failed intervention when it is an LR artifact. But LR decay is itself a candidate mechanism of critical-period closure, so the Week 4 pilot runs BOTH reset-alone AND reset+LR-spike as separate conditions to separate representation entrenchment from optimizer-schedule plasticity.

nodes.label: Standing Rule: No Premature Hardcoding
nodes.rationale: Checkpoint interval, total steps, and any step numbers derived from them are provisional until the Week 2 sanity run gives real totals. Keep them in one config location, label placeholders clearly, never scatter literals like 'if step % 500 == 0' across files.

nodes.label: Operational Definition: Circuit Identity
nodes.rationale: Repaired original circuit: activation patching at the baseline's relevant layers/heads reproduces skill behavior and ablating those components damages performance similarly to baseline. Built new circuit: patching/ablating baseline components has little effect on the recovered model.

nodes.label: Circuit Diagnosis Tooling (Week 8)
nodes.rationale: Activation patching/causal tracing, CKA/cosine representation similarity, ablation transfer test, pruning-based localization - built only once reopening is confirmed.

nodes.label: Tier 2 Fallback Intervention Methods
nodes.rationale: Only implemented if all 4 Tier 1 interventions show zero recovery: optimizer-state reset, cyclical LR restarts, adapter/LoRA modules, Net2Net growth, lottery-ticket rewind, spaced repetition, early-data replay, distillation from a healthy twin.

nodes.label: Week 3 Exit Gate: vocab-control signal check
nodes.rationale: Go/no-go before the Weeks 5-7 grid: run cloze_scores(per_word=True) on pilot checkpoints. Clean -> proceed; noisy but stable -> bump n_eval (cheap); still underpowered -> widen frequency band (expensive vocab scrub rebuild) - do it HERE, never mid-grid, because any change regenerates vocab.bin and eval numbers are only comparable between models trained on the same vocab.bin.
nodes.norm_label: week 3 exit gate: vocab-control signal check

nodes.label: Achille, Rovere & Soatto (2019) - Critical Learning Periods in Deep Neural Networks
nodes.author: Achille, Rovere & Soatto
nodes.rationale: Foundational paper: a temporary deficit (blurred images) early in a vision network's training causes permanent damage mirroring biological critical periods; the same deficit late in training is easily overcome. Deeper networks show the effect more strongly.
nodes.norm_label: achille, rovere & soatto (2019) - critical learning periods in deep neural networks

nodes.label: Kleinman, Achille & Soatto (2023/2024) - Multisensory integration & Deep linear networks
nodes.author: Kleinman, Achille & Soatto
nodes.rationale: CVPR 2023: multisensory integration depends on early exposure; early interference permanently impairs the skill via unstable early training dynamics. 2024 (arxiv 2308.12221): critical periods emerge even in deep LINEAR networks, suggesting a fundamental property of learning, not an architecture quirk.
nodes.norm_label: kleinman, achille & soatto (2023/2024) - multisensory integration & deep linear networks

nodes.label: Constantinescu et al. (2024) - Do Language Models Have a Critical Period for Language Acquisition?
nodes.author: Constantinescu, Pimentel, Cotterell & Warstadt
nodes.rationale: Directly relevant null result: LMs do not naturally show critical-period effects for delayed L2 exposure - human-like effects appeared only when plasticity was artificially reduced with EWC. The study directly engages this null; its setup (whole new language, post-hoc) differs from ours (specific skill within one language's pretraining).
nodes.norm_label: constantinescu et al. (2024) - do language models have a critical period for language acquisition?

nodes.label: Chen et al. (2023) - Improving Language Plasticity via Pretraining with Active Forgetting
nodes.author: Chen et al.
nodes.rationale: Basis for the embedding-reset intervention: periodically resetting the embedding layer as a standing pretraining policy gave faster adaptation to new languages. This study differs by applying reset retroactively as a rescue for a specific missed skill, within one language, and comparing against 3 alternative interventions plus circuit-level analysis.
nodes.norm_label: chen et al. (2023) - improving language plasticity via pretraining with active forgetting

nodes.label: Curriculum Learning for LLM Pretraining: An Analysis of Learning Dynamics (2026)
nodes.rationale: Closest to the syntax/timing angle: 14M-1B models under different data-ordering curricula follow shared latent phases; random ordering produces noisier gradients and worse final accuracy specifically in smaller models (14M-160M) - direct evidence that ordering matters at exactly this study's scale, in tension with Constantinescu's null result.
nodes.norm_label: curriculum learning for llm pretraining: an analysis of learning dynamics (2026)

nodes.label: Amblyopia-Treatment Analogy (paper hook)
nodes.rationale: The study mirrors amblyopia treatment in children - early-enough intervention can partially reverse vision loss from a missed critical window. Nobody has tested whether an analogous 'treatment' works for a missed skill window in LLM pretraining or looked inside the network to see how recovery happens.

nodes.label: Fisher Information mechanism of critical periods
nodes.rationale: Achille et al.'s explanatory mechanism: Fisher Information rises fast early in training then decreases, preventing later redistribution of information resources - why early deficits become permanent.
nodes.norm_label: fisher information mechanism of critical periods

nodes.label: Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC)
nodes.rationale: Regularizer that artificially reduces model plasticity; Constantinescu et al. only observed human-like critical-period effects when EWC was applied.

nodes.label: Curriculum-Design Motivation (applications angle)
nodes.rationale: Real multi-skill LLMs are one model trained on a designed mixture/curriculum - model merging does not reliably compose hierarchical knowledge. If delaying a skill past checkpoint X causes permanent capability loss, that is directly useful for curriculum ordering design; a motivating point for the paper, not a new experiment.

nodes.label: ML Primer for This Project
nodes.rationale: Math-background-assumed primer mapping ML vocabulary (loss, LR, Adam, tokens, embeddings, attention, layers, checkpoints, perplexity, activation patching, ablation, CKA) onto the exact pipeline pieces being built, so the researcher can sanity-check outputs without writing code.

nodes.label: Perplexity as safeguard metric
nodes.rationale: Perplexity = e^(average loss), how surprised the model is by real text. It is the safeguard metric: if an intervention raises skill accuracy but perplexity gets much worse, that is the catastrophic-forgetting pitfall, not real reopening.

nodes.label: Embedding layer (token ID -> vector lookup)
nodes.rationale: Lookup table from token ID to vector, shaped by training to encode meaning - which is why resetting it (intervention #1) is such a big deal: it wipes everything the model learned about representing every token.

nodes.label: Activation patching (primer definition)
nodes.rationale: Running the model normally but swapping in activations from a different run at one specific layer, to test whether that layer is causally responsible for a behavior.

nodes.label: Wh-Question Augmentation Sample
nodes.rationale: Generated review sample of recombined wh-question sentences (what/who/which + auxiliary inversion) produced by the syntax augmentation pipeline; exists for human spot-checking of grammaticality and naturalness of the augmented syntax-skill training data.

nodes.label: Achille, Rovere & Soatto (2019) — Critical Learning Periods in Deep Neural Networks
nodes.rationale: Theoretical foundation of the study: early temporary deficits (e.g. blurred images) cause permanent accuracy caps if applied during the early high-Fisher-Information plastic phase; the Detect phase tests whether the same delayed-exposure-causes-permanent-cap pattern appears for LLM skills.
nodes.norm_label: achille, rovere & soatto (2019) — critical learning periods in deep neural networks

nodes.label: Kleinman, Achille & Soatto (2023) — Multisensory Integration Critical Periods (CVPR)
nodes.rationale: Shows critical periods also govern learning to integrate multiple correlated input streams (audio+video), not just single-signal statistics; effect tied to instability in early training dynamics.
nodes.norm_label: kleinman, achille & soatto (2023) — multisensory integration critical periods (cvpr)

nodes.label: Kleinman, Achille & Soatto (2024) — Critical Periods in Deep Linear Networks
nodes.rationale: Critical periods appear even in linear networks with no nonlinearities, suggesting they are a fundamental consequence of gradient-based learning over time rather than a side-effect of architecture — strengthens the premise that LLMs should plausibly show them too.
nodes.norm_label: kleinman, achille & soatto (2024) — critical periods in deep linear networks

nodes.label: Constantinescu, Pimentel, Cotterell & Warstadt (2024) — Do Language Models Have a Critical Period for Language Acquisition?
nodes.rationale: Null result the study directly engages with: delayed L2 exposure caused no permanent cap in LLMs unless plasticity was artificially reduced with EWC. The null is specifically about cross-lingual whole-language transfer, not a specific skill introduced late within a single language's pretraining — the gap this research fills.
nodes.norm_label: constantinescu, pimentel, cotterell & warstadt (2024) — do language models have a critical period for language acquisition?

nodes.label: Chen et al. (2023) — Improving Language Plasticity via Pretraining with Active Forgetting
nodes.rationale: Direct methodological ancestor of intervention #1: periodically resetting the embedding layer throughout pretraining builds a meta-learning-like capacity for fast relearning of new languages. The study borrows the mechanism but applies it as a one-time targeted retroactive rescue for one missed skill, a meaningfully different and harder question.
nodes.norm_label: chen et al. (2023) — improving language plasticity via pretraining with active forgetting

nodes.label: Curriculum Learning for LLM Pretraining: An Analysis of Learning Dynamics (2026)
nodes.rationale: Hard evidence that data ordering has real, construction-specific effects on smaller models (14M-410M, the study's scale) without artificial plasticity damage — countering paper 3's implication that LLMs are immune to ordering effects. Verb Variation curriculum specifically improved wh-questions; curricula reallocate time among shared HMM-identified training phases rather than creating new ones.
nodes.norm_label: curriculum learning for llm pretraining: an analysis of learning dynamics (2026)

nodes.label: Critical Period (in neural network training)
nodes.rationale: A window early in training after which a delayed skill/signal becomes permanently harder to learn regardless of subsequent exposure. The study tests skill-specific, within-language critical periods in LLM pretraining — positioned between paper 3's cross-lingual null result and paper 5's construction-specific ordering effects.

nodes.label: Fisher Information (FI / FIM)
nodes.rationale: Proxy for how much the network can still be reshaped by new information: FI rises fast early (plastic phase), then drops and stabilizes (consolidation). Candidate diagnostic tool the study could borrow for its own analysis.

nodes.label: Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC)
nodes.rationale: Regularization penalizing changes to weights deemed important for existing knowledge; designed to prevent catastrophic forgetting. In paper 3 it artificially recreates a human-like critical period, illustrating that critical periods are connected to plasticity loss.

nodes.label: Gradient Noise Scale (GNS)
nodes.rationale: Measure of gradient inconsistency across mini-batches; paper 5 uses it to show random-ordering training is noisier than curriculum-ordered training in small models. Possible diagnostic for the study's own analysis.

nodes.label: Hidden Markov Model Latent Phase Analysis
nodes.rationale: Technique paper 5 fits to training trajectories to identify a shared sequence of training phases across data orderings; explains the claim that curricula reallocate time within existing phases rather than creating new ones.
nodes.norm_label: hidden markov model latent phase analysis

nodes.label: BLiMP (Benchmark of Linguistic Minimal Pairs)
nodes.rationale: Minimal-pair grammaticality benchmark: model scored on assigning higher probability to the grammatical sentence of a pair. This is how the study measures its syntax skill's accuracy.

nodes.label: Catastrophic Forgetting
nodes.rationale: Learning something new overwrites weights important for old capabilities. The study's key pitfall: recovering a delayed skill by damaging general language ability is catastrophic forgetting in disguise, not genuine reopening — hence dual-metric evaluation at every checkpoint.

nodes.label: Activation Patching / Causal Tracing
nodes.rationale: Main tool for the Diagnose phase: replace internal values at a chosen layer/head with values from a different run to test whether the recovered model relies on the same components as the original baseline.

nodes.label: Ablation
nodes.rationale: Disable/zero a network component and measure performance drop to establish whether that component was doing important work for the task.

nodes.label: CKA / Cosine Similarity
nodes.rationale: Representation-similarity measures for comparing hidden states across differently-trained models; used in the Diagnose phase to check whether the recovered model's internal representations resemble the baseline's.

nodes.label: Pruning-Based Localization
nodes.rationale: Find the smallest weight subset sufficient for a task; comparing pruned footprints of baseline vs recovered model reveals whether they rely on overlapping or entirely different parts of the network.

nodes.label: Mixed-Effects Regression
nodes.rationale: Statistical model separating fixed effects of interest (delay_onset, model_size) from random effects (seed, run) — the study's Week 9 analysis method for asking whether delay_onset predicts accuracy while accounting for run-to-run variation.

nodes.label: Held-Out Data
nodes.rationale: Evaluation data never seen in training; essential for every metric in the study (skill accuracy, general perplexity) to measure capability rather than memorization.

nodes.label: Embedding Reset Intervention (one-time rescue)
nodes.rationale: The study's leading intervention (#1): reset embeddings to fresh random init at one specific point after a skill's window has closed, then continue training. Borrows Chen et al.'s active-forgetting mechanism but as a single targeted retroactive fix rather than a standing all-along policy; Achille et al.'s note that the FI-drop 'forgetting' phase may be necessary for good representations is the conceptual justification for why deliberate forgetting could restore flexibility.

nodes.label: Wh-Question Object-Gap Extraction (syntax skill)
nodes.rationale: Chosen as the study's syntax skill because it is not arbitrary: paper 5's Verb Variation curriculum specifically improved wh-question performance, making it the one construction already shown to respond to data timing/ordering in prior work at the study's model scale. Measured via BLiMP-style minimal pairs.
